headword: ふるさと{納税|のうぜい}

definitions.explanation: A Japanese tax system that allows individuals to make donations to local governments of their choice in exchange for tax deductions and regional specialty gifts in return.

examples.japanese: ふるさと{納税|のうぜい}をした。
examples.english: I made a hometown tax donation.

examples.japanese: ふるさと{納税|のうぜい}の{返礼品|へんれいひん}でお{米|こめ}をもらった。
examples.english: I received rice as a return gift from the hometown tax program.

examples.japanese: {年末|ねんまつ}になると、ふるさと{納税|のうぜい}の{申|もう}し{込|こ}みが{増|ふ}える。
examples.english: Applications for the hometown tax donation program increase toward the end of the year.

notes:
FORMS:
ふるさと (hometown) + {納税|のうぜい} (tax payment)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Introduced in 2008 to help revitalize rural areas by allowing taxpayers to redirect a portion of their taxes to local governments outside their place of residence. Despite the name, it functions as a donation system rather than a direct tax. Donors receive {返礼品|へんれいひん} (return gifts) — typically regional specialties like meat, seafood, rice, or fruit — making it popular as a way to get local products while reducing taxes. Applications peak in December as people rush to make donations before the tax year ends.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ふるさと{納税|のうぜい}の{返礼品|へんれいひん}: return gift from hometown tax
- ふるさと{納税|のうぜい}を{申|もう}し{込|こ}む: to apply for hometown tax
- ふるさと{納税|のうぜい}サイト: hometown tax donation website
